jd_requirements: Motion control for actuator types (stepper, servo, brushed/brushless DC)
Robust perception/CV in high-speed low-latency applications

bullets.text: Developed embedded C firmware for STM32F407, enabling CAN-based motor control, BLE remote communication, and PID position control with +/-2 mm tracking error for an omnidirectional mobile robot.
Implemented a custom UART protocol with headers, footers, and float unpacking; used DMA + interrupts for non-blocking 100Hz updates of 6-DoF data, with <0.2% error rate.
Developed and tuned a dual-mode chassis control architecture with three PID loops managing translation and orientation, achieving <1.2s error convergence and 40% improvement in directional stability.
Designed a modular PID-based navigation system on STM32 with inverse kinematics and yaw compensation, achieving omnidirectional motion and +/-0.1% global localization accuracy.

Designed a compact, low-power crane system with ESP32-based Wi-Fi remote control, enabling low-latency communication and autonomous coordination across multiple devices, achieving over 95% task repeatability.
Independently developed an STM32-based control system using fuzzy PID algorithms for closed-loop stepper motor control, achieving +/-1 mm positioning accuracy.

Consolidated five functional boards into a single 4-layer PCB with KiCad, integrating control, power, and communication modules; reduced overall footprint by 40% and verified signal integrity via 100-MHz oscilloscope.
Designed a multi-servo gripper system with ultrasonic radar for 360-degree object detection, capable of grasping up to 3 objects simultaneously.

Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control in indoor environments.
Developed a ROS2-based robotic system integrating a simulator and MPC controller, enabling precise obstacle avoidance and full trajectory completion with real-time state logging.
Developed control programs for a six-axis CRP2 robotic arm using embedded C and ladder logic, enabling automated multi-axis motion for fuel rod testing.
Designed an STM32F103-based gateway to enable Modbus RTU communication between the PC and robotic controller, ensuring stable and real-time data exchange.

Proposed and implemented a magnetically-triggered encoder-based imaging system to replace low-precision pulse triggering, ensuring +/-1mm positional accuracy and reducing point-cloud data loss by 30%.
